about: Authored analytical workload for the datacharmer Employees sample. The source has no shipped views or application query workload.

queries.sql: SELECT d.dept_no, d.dept_name, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM dept_emp AS de JOIN departments AS d ON d.dept_no = de.dept_no WHERE de.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' GROUP BY d.dept_no, d.dept_name ORDER BY d.dept_no

SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(*) AS salary_rows, AVG(s.salary) AS average_salary FROM salaries AS s JOIN dept_emp AS de ON de.emp_no = s.emp_no AND de.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' JOIN departments AS d ON d.dept_no = de.dept_no WHERE s.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' GROUP BY d.dept_name
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM hire_date) AS hire_year, COUNT(*) AS hires FROM employees GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM hire_date)
SELECT title, COUNT(*) AS employees FROM titles WHERE to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' GROUP BY title
SELECT emp_no, from_date, salary, LAG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY emp_no ORDER BY from_date) AS previous_salary FROM salaries WHERE emp_no BETWEEN 10001 AND 10020
SELECT d.dept_name, m.emp_no, m.from_date, m.to_date FROM dept_manager AS m JOIN departments AS d ON d.dept_no = m.dept_no WHERE m.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01'

SELECT s.emp_no, s.salary FROM salaries AS s JOIN dept_emp AS de ON de.emp_no = s.emp_no AND de.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' WHERE s.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' AND s.salary > (SELECT AVG(s2.salary) FROM salaries AS s2 WHERE s2.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01')

SELECT e.emp_no, e.first_name, e.last_name, de.dept_no, t.title FROM employees AS e JOIN dept_emp AS de ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no JOIN titles AS t ON t.emp_no = e.emp_no WHERE de.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01' AND t.to_date = DATE '9999-01-01'
